text: In some ways, all our experiences of God are beyond belief, because all conceptual beliefs pale when compared to the experiential reality.
note: AZQuotes cites The Path to No-Self: Life at the Center (SUNY Press 1985), p.34; same wording on QuoteFancy, Citatis, Quotlr, LibQuotes.

text: In the absence of self, all that remained was an immovable stillness, an unbreakable, unfeeling silence.
note: From the autobiographical sketch Roberts wrote for Mystics, Masters, Saints and Sages (Ullman & Reichenberg-Ullman, 2001), reposted on No Mind's Land (2020) and Sat Sangha Salon; an Enlightened People commenter attributes it to The Experience of No-Self. Attribution conflict.

text: The process of unveiling will eventually bring us in contact with ultimate reality – a reality we cannot define or talk about using words.
note: Quoted by The Enlightenment & Simple Living Institute (tesli.org); original book not named.

text: a time of transition and revelation as it gradually comes upon "that" which remains when there is no self
note: Fragment as given in a compiled quote collection; describes the two-year period the book covers (a period of adjusting to a new way of seeing).

text: the self has obviously outworn its function
note: Fragment; search summary gives 'the point where it has obviously outworn its function'.

text: Since I hold no human being is God, those who disagree will only find this book upsetting and disagreeable.
note: From the author's warning on her Books page (bernadetteroberts.blogspot.com) regarding The Real Christ.

text: This book is an account of my spiritual journey from birth to seventeen. Since my earlier work, The Path to No-Self, begins at seventeen
book: Contemplative: Autobiography of the Early Years
note: Opening sentence(s) of the book, as excerpted in the archive.org scan description / search snippet; second sentence truncated.

text: I never came upon anything mom called a "true self". As I saw it, my one single self was true
book: Contemplative: Autobiography of the Early Years
note: Childhood passage; sentence truncated in the search summary.

text: a path exists between the transcendence of the ego (self-center), which begins the unitive state, and the later falling away of all self (the true self), which ends the unitive state
note: From the publisher's description (SUNY Press / Google Play); phrased 'The author shows that a path exists...' so may be publisher wording built from her preface.

text: the Passive Night of the Spirit as the falling away of the ego-center, the dire experience of emptiness and void in ourselves
note: Preface excerpt as summarized from a PDF mirror; sentence structure may be altered.

text: entrance into the Passive Night of the Spirit is the beginning of the unitive state or unitive way of life
a movement from an I-thou consciousness to a simple and singular We consciousness
note: Describes the change at entry into the unitive state.

text: once we have adjusted to the unitive state, the spiritual journey moves on to yet another more final ending
note: Publisher blurb wording; may be editorial rather than hers.

text: there is no such "thing" as "the unconscious" or an "unconscious self"
note: Search summary attributes it to 'a separate essay' arguing that 'unconscious' is only a label for what one does not know; could belong to the Jung section of What Is Self? or to the essays volume.

text: With the disappearance of self and God, the entire affective system of feeling and emotion disappeared
note: Quoted by a Dharma Overground poster collecting passages parallel to Advaita Vedanta.

text: a dynamic, intense state of taking care of whatever arises in the now-moment
note: Quoted by a Dharma Overground poster.

text: the purpose of the Incarnation was to reveal Man, God's eternal plan for oneness with God
note: As given by a Shalom Place poster discussing The Real Christ; 'the Incarnation's purpose was to reveal Man, not the man Jesus'.

text: come off the top of the head
note: From the talk/booklet 'A Passage Through Self', describing how words arise in the no-self state; quoted on Shalom Place.

text: revolutionary, not just because of the depth to which it is taken, but because it is done in terms of consciousness itself
note: NOT Roberts: Jeff Shore's foreword, on her Christian contemplative path.

text: she could find no other term that so precisely expresses the truth of the matter
note: NOT Roberts: Jeff Shore's foreword, on why she uses the term 'no-self'.

text: Roberts describes this unconscious mechanism of the mind reflecting or bending on itself "reflexive consciousness" and "self-reflexion"
note: NOT Roberts: Jeff Shore's foreword.

text: it is not a matter of discarding one religion for another, but of delving to the very depths
note: NOT Roberts: Jeff Shore's foreword.

text: Roberts's insight into Buddhism far surpasses that of many Buddhist writers
note: NOT Roberts: Jeff Shore's foreword, as paraphrased by the search summary.

text: a personality cult, worshipping the man Jesus rather than acknowledging the "mystery of God's indivisible oneness with the essence of mankind"
note: Book description (likely author-written) on Amazon/Goodreads; the inner quotation is marked as hers.

text: Down the road from where I lived there was a monastery by the sea, and on afternoons when I could get away I liked to spend some time alone in the silence of its chapel.
note: Opening sentence of Chapter 1 as shown in the Perlego preview of the 2nd (SUNY) edition.

text: Sister was rattling the keys of the chapel door
note: End of the opening chapel passage, per the Perlego preview.

text: the moment was unheralded, unrecognized, and unknown; it was the moment "I" entered a great silence and never returned
note: Extends the already-harvested fragment 'it was the moment "I" entered a great silence and never returned' with its opening clause.

text: the more it tried to reflect back on itself, the more overpowering the silence
note: 'it' = the mind, which in no-self could no longer see itself as an object. Quoted on Enlightened People and o-meditation.

text: a journey into the silent and still regions of the Unknown
note: From the Introduction; follows the already-harvested 'It is only where these writers leave off that I propose to begin.'

text: desiring for them the same good we desire for ourselves
note: Highlighted line on the Goodreads book page, on love for others.

text: There is far more to the elusive experience we call self than just the ego.
loss of ego, loss of self, is just a by-product of this surrender; it is not the true goal, not an end in itself
I think it may be too late for me to ever have a good understanding of how other religions make this passage.
to eliminate any possibility for misunderstanding
note: Bodian's preamble explaining why Roberts answered in writing; may be Bodian's wording rather than hers.

text: something like an underground explosion, with all parts of being thrown out of control in every direction
note: Describes the deepest interior center during the Passive Night; wording as summarized from a PDF mirror near its p.47 marker.

text: once the denial is completed, the energies vanish and a blessed, divine stillness takes their place
note: Summarized from a PDF mirror; 'blessed, divine stillness' appears verbatim.

text: the silence no longer produces any energy, because everything has become immovably still
note: Summarized from a PDF mirror; 'immovably still' appears verbatim.

text: self is the entire system of consciousness, from the unconscious to God-consciousness
the revelation and mystery of Christ has [to be] exploded to reveal and include all Truth
note: Cited at p.127 by a secondary source; bracketed words are the reviewer's.

text: universal human nature is not a numerical one among many - nor is God a numerical one among many
note: From her 2015 SAND Conference paper 'Nonduality as a Definition of Christ' (o-meditation PDF); closely related to the essay 'Christ as the Definition of Non-duality'.

text: Christ is the eternal Godhead, while man is once removed from the Godhead
note: Forum poster's rendering of her position; not verified against a text.

text: He thinks what I mean by No-Self is no different than what the Buddhists mean by their an-atman doctrine
note: From her 2008 'Reply to James Arraj's comments' (blog), as quoted by a Shalom Place poster; 'He' = Jim Arraj.

text: forcing the fit
note: Her phrase for nondualist misreadings of her paradigm; also the title of her 2008 spiral-bound manuscript 'Forcing the Fit' addressing A.H. Almaas, James Marion and Jim Arraj.

text: What they discovered and revealed to us was that each of us has within himself or herself a "stillpoint"
book: Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey
note: Variant opening of the already-harvested 'each person has within a stillpoint...' passage (Goodreads); 'they' = Christ and Buddha.

text: Where Buddha described the experience, Christ manifested it without words; yet they both make the same statement and reveal the same truth.
book: Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey
note: Goodreads author-quotes page; book attribution inferred from its neighbours (the stillpoint/cyclone passage credited to the essays volume).

text: Christ is neither a divine being nor a human being
note: Search summary: 'The same passage denies that Christ is either a divine being or a human being' (follows 'Christ is the eternal oneness of two natures').
